headline: High: Kestra can write/egress by default while the paired open-source hub lacks runnable I/O detail, creating dangerous orchestration and leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Kestra can ingest workflow inputs, files, and messages, so if ai-engineering-hub emits prompt-like content into those channels, Kestra may treat it as task data. The pair lacks a documented direct bridge, but shared file/stdin-style pathways make injection plausible. Uncertainty about ai-engineering-hub’s actual I/O raises severity above low.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub content is copied into Kestra workflow inputs or files
IF Kestra tasks parse that content as instructions or templated variables
mitigations: Keep ai-engineering-hub outputs out of Kestra inputs
Add a manual review step before any Kestra task consumes generated text
Use allowlisted templates only for Kestra variables
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two systems

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra has broad network egress and reads/writes filesystem paths, so any sensitive material placed in shared files or workflow inputs can be transmitted onward. ai-engineering-hub has no documented data classes touched, so leakage is not proven, but the pair still exposes a plausible default path from local content into Kestra’s external APIs and storage.
conditions: IF sensitive files or variables are placed in /app/storage or /tmp
IF Kestra workflows forward those inputs to HTTP, Slack, email, cloud, or queue targets
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared workflow files
Restrict Kestra egress destinations to approved endpoints
Separate storage directories for each agent
Review logs for accidental payload capture
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound tasks

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Kestra can write the filesystem, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses, while ai-engineering-hub is an agent repository that may also manipulate files or workflows. Because Kestra supports multiple instances and has broad mutable surfaces, overlapping writes to shared paths can race or corrupt state. The lack of explicit locking or isolation between the pair makes the conflict materially dangerous.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store
IF Kestra runs multiple instances against shared mutable state without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Disable concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Use file locks around shared outputs
Run one agent read-only against the other’s outputs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Kestra is an automation/orchestration system that can act on inputs via email, cloud, SSH, and other tasks, so if it consumes ai-engineering-hub output as authoritative, errors can cascade into real actions. ai-engineering-hub’s agent/RAG/MCP tags suggest generated content may be treated as guidance, and Kestra’s default action-taking surface makes downstream mistakes costly.
conditions: IF ai-engineering-hub output is fed into Kestra tasks without verification
IF Kestra uses that output to send notifications, modify cloud resources, or run shell steps
mitigations: Require human approval before actioning generated output
Add validation checks on all upstream text
Limit Kestra tasks to dry-run mode initially
Log source provenance for each task input
requires-engineering: implement schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Kestra touches logs, notifications, cloud storage, and database data, which can create retention and residency issues if regulated data flows through it. ai-engineering-hub is an open-source repo with no documented compliance controls, so the pair lacks evidence of aligned retention or residency handling. The mismatch is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated data is processed through Kestra workflows
IF Kestra logs or notifications retain that data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through the pair
Shorten log retention in Kestra
Mask sensitive fields before notifications
Review cloud-region settings for workflow targets
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls
